body:
### Summary

While investigating an AugeLab Studio installation failure, we observed uv 0.9.17 rejecting a large dependency wheel during metadata resolution through our public CloudFront-backed package index. Resolving with the same object's public S3-origin URL succeeded.

The failure is `Failed to read from zip file`, reported as an invalid package format / unsatisfiable dependency. We have not established whether the cause is HTTP delivery, ZIP streaming/validation, or another uv behavior. This is not a claim that CloudFront or uv is definitively at fault.

### Environment and limitations

- Reproduction host: Windows x86_64, CPython 3.12.8.
- uv: `0.9.17 (2b5d65e61 2025-12-09)`.
- Resolution target: `--python-version 3.12 --python-platform aarch64-manylinux_2_35`.
- These are dependency-resolution dry runs, not execution of ARM64 code on Windows.
- Observations collected September 11, 2026. We have not yet repeated the failure on current uv (0.12.13 at filing time).
- A customer originally reported an Ubuntu 22.04 ARM64 installation problem, but their installer logs do NOT contain the ZIP-read error below. It was reproduced separately during investigation. Their unrelated APT errors and identifying information are omitted.

### Public artifact

Index: https://pyrepo.augelab.com/augelab-extra-modules/

CDN wheel:
https://pyrepo.augelab.com/augelab-extra-modules/augelab_extra_modules-3.0.0-cp312-none-any.whl

S3-origin wheel:
https://studio-desktop-repo-v3.s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/augelab-extra-modules/augelab_extra_modules-3.0.0-cp312-none-any.whl

The wheel is **1,563,651,157 bytes**. The URLs are public and require no credentials. Please account for the download size when reproducing.

### Observed failing command

The command below is the full tested resolution request, with only the local target path replaced by a relative diagnostic directory. A smaller package-only reproduction has not yet been confirmed.

```powershell
uv --no-config pip install --dry-run --target ./uv-cdn-probe --python-version 3.12 --python-platform aarch64-manylinux_2_35 --index-url https://pypi.org/simple --extra-index-url https://pyrepo.augelab.com --index-strategy unsafe-best-match --torch-backend cpu "studio[ui,gpu]==3.10.0" -v
```

Selected verbose output (unrelated dependency enumeration and local cache paths omitted):

```text
DEBUG Selecting: studio==3.10.0 [compatible] (studio-3.10.0-cp312-none-any.whl)
DEBUG No cache entry for: https://pyrepo.augelab.com/augelab-extra-modules/augelab_extra_modules-3.0.0-cp312-none-any.whl
WARN Range requests not supported for augelab_extra_modules-3.0.0-cp312-none-any.whl; streaming wheel
WARN augelab-extra-modules==3.0.0 has an invalid package format: Failed to read from zip file
WARN augelab-extra-modules has an invalid package format: Failed to read from zip file
  × No solution found when resolving dependencies:
  ╰─▶ Because augelab-extra-modules==3.0.0 has an invalid package format and
      studio[gpu]==3.10.0 depends on augelab-extra-modules==3.0.0, we can
      conclude that studio[gpu]==3.10.0 cannot be used.
      And because you require studio[gpu]==3.10.0, we can conclude that your
      requirements are unsatisfiable.

      hint: The structure of `augelab-extra-modules` (v3.0.0) was invalid:
        Failed to read from zip file
```

Exit status: 1.

### Successful comparison

```powershell
uv --no-config pip install --dry-run --target ./uv-origin-probe --python-version 3.12 --python-platform aarch64-manylinux_2_35 --index-url https://pypi.org/simple --extra-index-url https://pyrepo.augelab.com --index-strategy unsafe-best-match --torch-backend cpu "studio[ui,gpu]==3.10.0" "PySide6==6.8.0.2" "augelab-extra-modules @ https://studio-desktop-repo-v3.s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/augelab-extra-modules/augelab_extra_modules-3.0.0-cp312-none-any.whl"
```

Selected output:

```text
Resolved 197 packages in 3.34s
Would download 115 packages
Would install 197 packages
 + augelab-extra-modules @ https://studio-desktop-repo-v3.s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/augelab-extra-modules/augelab_extra_modules-3.0.0-cp312-none-any.whl
 + studio==3.10.0
```

Exit status: 0. This comparison also adds an explicit Qt requirement, so it is not a strict single-variable experiment. The failure excerpt specifically identifies the extra-modules wheel, and independent inspection below also succeeded at the origin.

### HTTP and ZIP inspection

```powershell
curl.exe -fsSI --range -65536 https://pyrepo.augelab.com/augelab-extra-modules/augelab_extra_modules-3.0.0-cp312-none-any.whl
curl.exe -fsSI --range -65536 https://studio-desktop-repo-v3.s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/augelab-extra-modules/augelab_extra_modules-3.0.0-cp312-none-any.whl
```

Selected CDN HEAD response:

```text
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/octet-stream
Content-Length: 1563651157
ETag: "bda783a393db1b9f44d6eff963f7abde-187"
Server: AmazonS3
X-Cache: Hit from cloudfront
```

Selected S3 HEAD response:

```text
HTTP/1.1 206 Partial Content
ETag: "bda783a393db1b9f44d6eff963f7abde-187"
Accept-Ranges: bytes
Content-Range: bytes 1563585621-1563651156/1563651157
Content-Length: 65536
```

These are HEAD observations; the CDN response alone does not prove that ranged GET requests are unsupported. Python `zipfile.ZipFile` using a seekable reader backed by ranged GET requests to S3 successfully read the central directory and METADATA:

```text
Metadata-Version: 2.1
Name: augelab-extra-modules
Version: 3.0.0
Summary: augelab project
Author-email: AugeLab Tech <info@augelab.com>
Requires-Python: >=3.12
```

This validates access to ZIP metadata, not every payload entry or a complete installation. Matching ETags are supporting evidence, not a full independently computed content-hash comparison.

### Expected behavior / question

If possible, fall back to a non-streaming metadata read when streaming fails, or expose the underlying ZIP/HTTP error so an artifact-format problem can be distinguished from a transport failure. Is this consistent with a known problem fixed after 0.9.17, or is there a particular ZIP property or HTTP trace we should investigate?

Possibly related: #21349 (range detection/full-wheel downloads) and #18688 (direct-URL streaming fallback). We have not confirmed this is the same issue.

Disclosure: diagnostics and this evidence report were prepared with an AI coding assistant at the reporter's request. Command outputs above come from actual tool executions; uncertainties and untested steps are stated explicitly.
title: uv 0.9.17: large wheel metadata ZIP-read failure via CloudFront, resolution succeeds via S3 origin
